# Florence 1490 – Communication & information

K = knowledge level · use = none/wrong/partial/correct · make = producibility with local means · accept = acceptance.

- **Writing (signs that record language)** [`writing_invention`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/writing_invention.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high
- **Alphabet and mass literacy** [`alphabet_writing`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/alphabet_writing.md) — K4, use partial, make easy, accept high. Florence is unusually literate: most merchants' and artisans' sons read and write Tuscan. Peasants and most women do not.
- **Codex book and finding aids** [`codex_book`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/codex_book.md) — K4, use partial, make easy, accept high. Books have leaf numbers at best; page numbers, title pages and alphabetical indexes are rare in print. An easy improvement for printers. Local: Vespasiano da Bisticci (retired bookseller); cartolai (stationers).
- **Woodblock printing** [`woodblock_printing`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/woodblock_printing.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept high. Used for playing cards, saints' images, cloth patterns and book illustration; Florentine woodcut books begin about 1490. Whole-page text blocks are a northern habit. Elsewhere: Germany and the Netherlands, block books; China and Korea, extensive woodblock printing.
- **Movable-type printing press** [`printing_press`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/printing_press.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Florence has had presses since 1471 and printed the first Greek Homer (1488). Venice dominates the trade. Pamphlets spread ideas fast, and accusations too. Local: Antonio Miscomini; Bartolomeo de' Libri; Lorenzo Morgiani. Elsewhere: Venice: the largest printing centre in Europe.
- **Reproducing images (woodcut, engraving, etching, lithography)** [`lithography_engraving`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/lithography_engraving.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept high. Woodcut and copper engraving flourish (goldsmiths' craft); used for devotional images and maps, hardly for technical drawings. Etching on paper and lithography are unknown. Local: Francesco Rosselli; goldsmiths (niello work). Elsewhere: Rome, Antonio del Pollaiuolo; Mantua, Mantegna; Upper Rhine, Schongauer.
- **Relay post and public mail** [`postal_system`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/postal_system.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept high. Merchant guild couriers (scarsella) leave on fixed days for Lyon, Bruges, Rome, Venice; princes run relay riders. Nothing is open to the public at a fixed price. Local: Mercanzia and merchant companies' couriers. Elsewhere: Milan: Sforza relay post; 1490: the Tassis family starts Maximilian's Innsbruck–Netherlands relay.
- **Newspapers and periodicals** [`newspapers_periodicals`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/newspapers_periodicals.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept medium. News travels in merchants' letters and ambassadors' dispatches, copied and passed on. A regular printed sheet is new; rulers will want to control it. Local: printers; bankers' correspondence networks.
- **Scientific journal and peer review** [`scientific_journal`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/scientific_journal.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept low. Humanists exchange Latin letters, some printed. A periodical would require a printer, a continuing supply of reports and readers willing to support it.
- **Encyclopedias and dictionaries** [`encyclopedia_reference_works`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/encyclopedia_reference_works.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept high. Pliny (in Landino's Italian, 1476), Isidore and Vincent of Beauvais are the reference works: unverified, not alphabetical, and silent on workshop practice. Local: Cristoforo Landino; printers.
- **Library catalogue and classification** [`library_catalogue`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/library_catalogue.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Libraries have inventories by desk and subject, with books chained to benches. Slips, shelf marks per volume and author indexes are new. Local: San Marco library; Medici library. Elsewhere: Rome: Vatican Library inventories (Platina, 1475–81).
- **Pencil, steel pen and durable ink** [`pencil_steel_pen`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/pencil_steel_pen.md) — K1, use none, make medium, accept high. Artists draw with silverpoint, lead stylus, chalk and charcoal; everyone writes with quill and iron-gall ink. Graphite is not known as a material. Local: painters' workshops; goldsmiths (could cut metal nibs).
- **Shorthand (stenography)** [`shorthand`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/shorthand.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept high. Humanists have heard of Cicero's Tironian notes. Notaries use heavy abbreviation; sermons are reconstructed from hurried notes. Local: Arte dei Giudici e Notai; listeners taking down Savonarola's sermons.
- **Typewriter** [`typewriter`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/typewriter.md) — K0, use none, make very-hard, accept low
- **Copying documents (copying press, carbon paper, stencil duplicator)** [`copying_duplicating`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/copying_duplicating.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept high. Every merchant letter is copied by hand into a copy-book by a clerk. Lampblack, wax, oil and thin paper exist. Local: merchant-banking houses; chancery of the Signoria.
- **Braille (tactile writing for blind people)** [`braille_tactile_writing`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/braille_tactile_writing.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept medium. The blind live as beggars or singers.
- **Sign languages of deaf people** [`sign_languages`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/sign_languages.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept medium. The deaf are held unteachable. Monks know sign lists for hours of silence.
- **Knowledge in the vernacular; translation movements** [`vernacular_translation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/vernacular_translation.md) — K4, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Tuscan is a literary language (Dante; Landino's Pliny; printed Italian Bible, 1471). Medicine, law, theology and university teaching stay Latin; Greek science is being translated into Latin. Local: Cristoforo Landino; abacus-school textbooks.
- **Beacons, flag codes and heliograph** [`signal_beacons_flag_codes`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/signal_beacons_flag_codes.md) — K4, use partial, make easy, accept high. Fortresses and coast towers pass pre-agreed alarms by fire, smoke and bells. No code for arbitrary messages.
- **Optical telegraph (semaphore network)** [`optical_telegraph`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/optical_telegraph.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept high. Signal fires and towers exist for war. A coded semaphore line between Florence and Pisa would be militarily valuable; without telescopes the stations must stand close.
- **Standard time and time zones** [`standard_time_zones`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/standard_time_zones.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept low. Town clocks follow local time. Pisa and Florence could agree on a common reference and compare readings periodically. Keeping clocks synchronized would take continuing work.
